solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member of choir is b—- fool

parts.note: the letter b is taken as printed, the dashes standing in for a word left unsaid
an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A chorister is dismissed as a blankety-blank fool, the rude word discreetly dashed out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes look like a censored swearword, but only the letter b counts, with the fool following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a singer with the lowest male voice part, one of the standard sections of a choir.

clue.text: Journey with one yet to pass test is rubbish

parts.note: a drive is a journey by car
L for learner, a driver who has not yet passed the driving test

explanation.surface: A trip with a learner who has yet to pass the driving test goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate shown by British drivers who have not passed their test.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is nonsense, silly talk, which is what 'rubbish' means when said of what someone says.

clue.text: Maiden, possibly sweetheart losing head

indicators.note: a word losing its head drops its first letter

parts.note: a sweetheart is a lover

explanation.surface: A young maiden might, perhaps, find her sweetheart has lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman, but in cricket a maiden is a set of six balls from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is one example of a cricket over, hence 'possibly' to mark the definition by example.

clue.text: A writer's absorbing article

parts.note: surface reading: a gripping piece by an author
setter's reading: an item that soaks up ink for someone writing with a pen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' reads as fascinating and 'article' as a magazine piece; really it is a literal object that soaks up wet ink.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick porous sheet is pressed onto fresh ink to dry it, so it is an object that literally absorbs for writers.

clue.text: A fraud I am after, alternatively

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
post is Latin for after, as in postwar
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they might be after a fraudster, or something else entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone else to deceive, so is a fraud in the sense of a person, not a scheme.

clue.text: They may be obtuse, but they also may be right

definitions.text: They may be obtuse, but they also may be right

parts.words: They may be obtuse, but they also may be right
parts.note: surface reading: people who can be dim-witted yet sometimes correct
setter's reading: obtuse and right are both terms from geometry describing a turn between two lines

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a remark about stupid people who are nonetheless correct; both adjectives are geometry words.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry these measures between lines are classed as acute, right (90 degrees) or obtuse (over 90 degrees).

clue.text: Member of clan — one to wake up the folk in tents?

parts.note: a camp is a group of people living in tents
a bell is rung to wake people

explanation.surface: A clansman is cast as the person whose job is rousing everyone sleeping under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order to the clue: the folk in tents first, then the wake-up call.
explanation.definitionFit: The Campbells are a famous Scottish Highland clan, so anyone bearing that surname belongs to it.

clue.text: A king and enemy coming on the scene

parts.note: taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king
a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A monarch and his foe make their entrance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of turning up, so a noun phrase for appearing somewhere fits it.

clue.text: Fellow going to North America for super food

parts.note: a fellow is a man
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A man travels to America in search of so-called superfoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super food' looks like a modern health fad; here super means heavenly, supernatural.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna is the miraculous bread from heaven that fed the Israelites in the Bible, food from above.

clue.text: Cut flower short

indicators.note: falling short means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Severn is Britain's longest

explanation.surface: A gardener trims a bloom down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is a flow-er, a river. The Severn runs through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through or cut off, a direct synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Victorian writer reported disreputable female

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

parts.note: Anthony Trollope, the Victorian novelist of the Barsetshire books

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist was said to keep low company.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is an old-fashioned insult for a promiscuous or slovenly woman.

clue.text: Painter and inventor in Italy's capital

indicators.note: a word's capital is its opening letter, so only the start of the place is used

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone
taken as written
the first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: An artist and an inventor turn up in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's capital' suggests Rome, but it is just the first letter of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Bellini was a leading Venetian Renaissance painter, so his surname names an artist.

clue.text: Brought up to hide pain, being violated

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: bred means raised, brought up
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone raised to conceal their pain suffers an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or a wall that is breached has been broken through, which is what violated means here.

clue.text: Maybe Spanish folks and Russians, heading off

indicators.note: with the heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Siberians are Russians from Siberia

explanation.surface: Spanish people and Russians set off on a journey together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like departing; it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula holds Spain and Portugal, so Spaniards are an example of its people, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Sample latest of paintings in gallery

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its most recent, final letter

parts.note: the last letter of paintings

explanation.surface: Try out the newest paintings on show at a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste is to sample, try a little of something, as a verb.

clue.text: Supply to last, right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed from the word

parts.note: to endure is to last
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Provisions are meant to last, so get them sent off straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is a formal verb meaning to provide or endow someone with a quality.

clue.text: Most awful French art covered in muck

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by something else on both sides

parts.note: dirt is muck
tu es is French for 'you art', the old form of 'you are'

explanation.surface: The worst French paintings are smeared in filth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' looks like painting; it is the old verb form 'thou art' in French, es.
explanation.definitionFit: Direst is the superlative of dire, meaning terrible, so it means most awful.

clue.text: Gloria's unusual gem

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their normal order

parts.note: the name with its S

explanation.surface: A woman named Gloria owns a rare jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Girasol is a kind of opal that shows a bluish glow, a precious stone.

clue.text: Japanese money had for governing body

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese coin
to have a meal is to eat, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: Japanese cash was taken by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, the upper house of parliament in many countries.

clue.text: A croc is swimming somewhere in the Med!

indicators.note: swimming means moving about, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alarm on the beach: a crocodile has been seen in the Mediterranean!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb of the sentence, but its letters join the fodder: A CROC IS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean Sea, an example of a place there.

clue.text: First in class, little Andrew is sweet

indicators.note: first in means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of class
Andy is the short form of Andrew

explanation.surface: Young Andrew, top of the class, is a lovely child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective about Andrew; it is the noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is a sweet, a sugary confection, the American word for it.

clue.text: Gang somewhere in Cheshire, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is judged by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: Word has it a gang is operating in a Cheshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group working together, or informally a gang of friends.

clue.text: Time that is long needing to be shortened

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, losing the final letter

parts.note: to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: A period that is too long and needs trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about time; it is the verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, twelve months.

clue.text: Half of the things you really need in German city

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just its first five of ten letters

parts.note: the first half of essentials, the things you really need

explanation.surface: Packing advice: take only half of what you think you truly need.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Classical female appearing in select range

indicators.note: appearing in means sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs from the second letter of select into the start of range

explanation.surface: A woman from antiquity turns up in an exclusive product line.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a figure from Greek myth and tragedy, daughter of Agamemnon, a female of classical literature.
